title: Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) via Unsanitized href in UrlField
analysis: Data Path: - Source: Untrusted data from a data provider (e.g., API response, database records, CSV upload, or URL search query parameters like '?source=...') containing user-controlled fields. - Sanitization/Validation: None. UrlField extracts the field value from the record via `get(record, source)` and performs no sanitization or URL scheme validation (such as ensuring the URL begins with a safe scheme like 'http://' or 'https://' or blocking 'javascript:'). - Sink: The unsanitized URL string is passed directly to Material UI's `` component on line 36, which renders an HTML `` tag with the user-controlled `href` attribute. Impact: When an administrator or user views a record with a malicious URL and clicks the link in a list or detail view, the `javascript:` payload executes in the victim's browser session with the victim's privileges. This enables stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS), session hijacking, and arbitrary actions within the admin interface. Conceptual Exploit Payload: A record stored in the backend database or returned by a REST/GraphQL endpoint containing: ```json { "id": 123, "website": "javascript:alert(document.domain)" } ``` When rendered with ``, the component generates: ```html javascript:alert(document.domain) ``` Clicking the link triggers script execution in the context of the application.

title: Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) via Unsanitized href in FileField
analysis: Data Path: - Source: Untrusted data from a data provider (e.g., API response, database records, CSV import) containing file URL values. - Sanitization/Validation: None. FileField retrieves `sourceValue` from `record` via `get(record, source)` and performs no protocol check or scheme validation (e.g. against 'javascript:' pseudoprotocols). - Sink: The unsanitized value is converted to string and supplied directly as the `href` prop of Material UI's `` component on line 95 (and similarly line 72 for array fields), which renders an HTML `` tag. Impact: When an administrator clicks the link intended to download or view a file, a malicious `javascript:` URI executes script in the user's browser, leading to stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS). Conceptual Exploit Payload: A record stored in the backend database: ```json { "id": 1, "attachment": "javascript:alert(document.domain)", "title": "Invoice.pdf" } ``` When rendered with ``, the component generates: ```html Invoice.pdf ``` Clicking the file link executes the JavaScript code in the user's browser context.

title: Improper URL Validation via Missing Anchor in UrlRegexp leading to Type Inference Bypass
analysis:
Data Path:
- Source: Untrusted data strings from API endpoints, databases, or user-uploaded CSV files processed by type inference mechanisms (used in ListGuesser, ShowGuesser, EditGuesser, and ra-no-code).
- Sanitization/Validation: `assertions.ts` defines `UrlRegexp = /http(s*):\/\/.*/i` to validate whether string values represent URLs. The regular expression lacks start anchors (`^`), meaning any string containing `http://` or `https://` anywhere within it will match `isUrl(value)` and pass `valuesAreUrl(values)`. Furthermore, `(s*)` matches zero or more 's' characters arbitrarily.
- Sink: When `valuesAreUrl(values)` evaluates to `true`, `inferTypeFromValues` assigns the element type as `'url'`. In `ListGuesser`, `ShowGuesser`, and `ra-no-code`, elements typed as `'url'` are rendered using `<UrlField>`, which passes the string directly into `<Link href={value}>` without sanitization, leading to arbitrary JavaScript execution when the resulting link is clicked.

Impact:
An attacker can craft malicious payload strings such as `javascript:alert(1)//https://example.com` in data records. Because `UrlRegexp` is unanchored, the validation logic erroneously classifies the field as a valid URL instead of a plain string (`TextField`), causing guessers and no-code components to generate clickable links containing JavaScript execution payloads.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
A data record containing a custom property:
```json
{
  "id": 1,
  "custom_link": "javascript:alert(document.cookie)//https://example.com"
}
```
Evaluating `UrlRegexp.test("javascript:alert(document.cookie)//https://example.com")` returns `true`. `inferTypeFromValues('custom_link', [...])` returns `{ type: 'url', props: { source: 'custom_link' } }`, which `ListGuesser` renders as `<UrlField source="custom_link" />`, yielding an executable JavaScript link.
